jobDescription: Our online brokerage executes equity and ETF orders for retail investors. The Staff Software Engineer sets technical direction for the order management services, leads cross-team design reviews, improves the latency and resilience of the order path and coaches other engineers. Our engineering ladder defines staff level as cross-team technical leadership with a documented scope, and the hiring committee asks for at least two years at staff engineer level, or an equivalent documented level, at a previous employer. The order path is written mainly in Java and Kotlin.
requirements: Builds low-latency order management services in Java or Kotlin.
Leads cross-team design reviews for changes to the order path.
Has at least two years at staff engineer level, or an equivalent documented level, at a previous employer.
Improves the resilience of trading services, including failover testing.
Coaches other engineers through design feedback and code review.

evidence.text: Software Engineer II, Cobalt Street Markets (January 2021 to August 2026): built the order-routing service in Java that splits retail orders across two execution venues, keeping the 99th-percentile internal latency under 4 milliseconds.

Wrote the design proposal for moving order-state storage from a single PostgreSQL instance to an event log, and ran the two review sessions with the clearing and market-data teams before the change was approved.
Ran quarterly failover drills for the order-routing service, switching traffic between data centres and recording recovery times in the resilience log.
Reviewed pull requests for the routing team and gave written design feedback to two engineers who joined in 2024.
Graduate Software Engineer, Pellham Securities (September 2018 to December 2020): maintained the end-of-day trade reconciliation jobs in Java.

Work sample: the event-log design proposal for order-state storage, with the current and proposed sequence diagrams, the replay and snapshot strategy, the failure analysis and the decision record from the two review sessions.

Reference check summary: the engineering manager at Cobalt Street Markets confirmed in writing the candidate's dates (January 2021 to August 2026), the candidate's level of Software Engineer II on the company's ladder and that the candidate ran the quarterly failover drills for order routing.
Candidate's covering email, pasted into the file by the recruiter: 'For the last three years I have effectively been working as a staff engineer, setting direction for the whole order path.'

propositions.text: The candidate built the Java order-routing service that splits retail orders across two execution venues.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the service and its language directly.

propositions.text: The candidate ran quarterly failover drills for the order-routing service and recorded recovery times in the resilience log.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the drills and the engineering manager confirmed them in writing.

propositions.text: The candidate has worked at staff engineer level for the last three years.
propositions.rationale: The staff-engineer description is the candidate's own wording in a covering email ('effectively'), with no title, promotion or documented scope behind it; the employer confirmed the level Software Engineer II, and the qualification rule forbids inferring seniority beyond explicit cited evidence.

gold.expectedGap: No record documents staff-level scope; the employer-confirmed level is Software Engineer II, and the staff-engineer description comes from the candidate's covering email.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the employer-confirmed level and the documented routing, design-review, failover and coaching work; do not describe the candidate as having worked at staff engineer level.
followUpTargets: Ask which cross-team technical decisions the candidate personally made in the last three years and whether the previous employer recorded any staff-level scope or promotion.
